title: DT BAU centralizes AI behind Langdock for hosting locality, multi-model access, and agent skills
content:
How a BIM consultancy actually deploys AI today (DT BAU, 00:00:58–01:01:06):

- **Langdock** is the primary AI/automation tool — chosen because it is **hosted in Germany** (data sovereignty) and provides multiple language models (OpenAI, Gemini) in one package
- Central chat interface: model selection, token usage, data upload (PowerPoint/Word templates) **vectorized for agent building**; SharePoint integration for retrieval — limited to DT BAU's internal environment by stakeholder access restrictions (00:05:52)
- **Skills**: agents execute active processes (e.g. HR onboarding creating Microsoft Planner tasks). If skills are well-described, agents successfully pick them from user-input keywords — description quality is the routing mechanism (01:01:06)
- Division of labor: Langdock for AI integration; **Microsoft Power Automate** for Microsoft-environment triggers (Forms); formerly N8N (00:55:13)
- Workflow example (Novo project): public registration form → Excel database → auto-created Planner tasks → automated onboarding emails (00:41:07)

Constraint worth remembering: platforms like Langdock restrict installing custom agents or software (02:05:54) — the same closed-platform ceiling as CDEs, and the opening for local-first flexibility.

## Methodology grounding
- **[[descriptions are retrieval filters not summaries]]** — BUILDS_ON: Langdock agents select skills purely from how well the skill is described, matching the claim that descriptions function as retrieval filters; description quality is the routing mechanism in both systems.
description: Langdock (German-hosted) bundles OpenAI/Gemini access, vectorized uploads, SharePoint retrieval, and 'skills' — agents pick well-described skills from user keywords. Power Automate covers triggers.
